summary: A 1942 Aermotor tower built at Old Bridge under the wartime security program, moved to Thompson Park in 1963 as the Jamesburg Station fire tower.

facts.design: LS-42 60-foot Aermotor steel tower, 48 ft to the cab floor
facts.agency: New Jersey Forest Fire Service, Division B

events.note: Erected at Old Bridge as the Old Bridge fire tower under the wartime home-front security program
Moved to Thompson Park, Monroe Township, Middlesex County, becoming the Jamesburg Station fire tower
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, March 3, 2004, nominated by Bob Spear

evidence.supports: built 1942 at Old Bridge under wartime security program
evidence.quote: Originally erected as the Old Bridge fire tower in 1942 under the wartime security program, this LS-42 60’ Aermotor tower may even have an as yet unconfirmed earlier life dating to 1924.

evidence.supports: moved 1963 to present site, active service

notes_for_editor: Record's 'built 1942' matches NHLR, but that date is for the original Old Bridge tower; the structure was relocated to the current Jamesburg site in 1963, which the record's events list omits. The nomination's claim of a possible 1924 origin is explicitly unconfirmed. Current access/staffing/rental status could not be confirmed from a quotable primary source within budget; a WebSearch summary suggested climbing is allowed only when Forest Fire Service staff are present, but I could not verify that against an actual page I read, so it is left out of facts/events and the record's 'access: unknown' stands.
